```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Figures: scripts/79_ecofuel_figs.R (figs/<figure>_<profile>.png + manifest.csv). Tables: 79 copies
# 71's inventory to tables/ecofuel_<table>_<profile>.csv. The CONUS ("full") version is shown when
# it exists, otherwise the dev one.
figs <- if (file.exists("figs/manifest.csv")) {
  utils::read.csv("figs/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else data.frame(figure = character(), profile = character())

show_fig <- function(name, caption, alt = caption) {
  m <- figs[figs$figure == name, , drop = FALSE]
  pick <- intersect(c("full", "dev"), m$profile)
  pick <- pick[file.exists(sprintf("figs/%s_%s.png", name, pick))]
  if (!length(pick)) {
    cat(sprintf('\n::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n## Figure pending\n%s\n:::\n\n', caption))
    return(invisible())
  }
  r <- m[m$profile == pick[1], ][1, ]
  note <- sprintf("[%s · %s · figure made %s]{.fig-meta}", r$extent, r$years, r$made)
  cat(sprintf('\n![%s %s](figs/%s_%s.png){#fig-%s fig-alt="%s" .column-page-right}\n\n',
              caption, note, name, pick[1], gsub("_", "-", name), alt))
}
tab <- function(name) {
  for (p in c("full", "dev")) {
    f <- sprintf("tables/ecofuel_%s_%s.csv", name, p)
    if (file.exists(f)) { x <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = c(code = "character")); attr(x, "profile") <- p; return(x) }
  }
  NULL
}
E <- tab("ecoregions"); U <- tab("units")
have <- !is.null(E) && !is.null(U)
prof_note <- if (have && attr(E, "profile") == "dev") " (Arizona test area only; CONUS run pending)" else ""
burn <- c("GR", "GS", "SH", "TU", "TL")
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Exploration in progress, October 2026
This page records a new piece of work: whether green-up and curing climatologies (and possibly
models) can be built for units fire managers already use, **EPA Level II ecoregions × LANDFIRE fuel
types**. It is a companion to the [fuel phenology regions page](index.html); it reads the
[NPN curing study](npn_study.html)'s site tables and the [fire study](fire_study.html)'s fire
records but changes neither. Nothing below is a decision yet: the first step is an inventory of
the candidate units, to settle the open questions before any climatology is built.
:::

## Why ecoregions × fuel types

- **Operational fit.** Fire danger rating grids are built on fuel models (Scott & Burgan 40,
  mapped by LANDFIRE), and ecoregions are units managers already know. A table of
  "ecoregion × fuel group → typical green-up, peak and curing dates, with their spread" can be
  used directly.
- **Evidence for climatologies.** The NPN curing study found that place explains most of the
  variation in ground green-up and curing dates, and no weather model beat the typical date. The
  regions work found the same at the ground almost everywhere except the monsoon Southwest and
  California annual grasslands.
- **Independent units.** Level II ecoregions and LANDFIRE are published layers, chosen without
  any of the phenology data, so testing them against the ground dates is not circular.

## How the units are built (steps 1–2)

1. **Fuel models on the 4 km grid.** The LANDFIRE 2023 FBFM40 map (30 m) is summarised into the
   share of each of the 40 fuel models, and of each nonburnable class (agriculture, urban, water,
   barren, snow), in every 4 km cell of the analysis grid: first in about 1 km blocks, then
   area-averaged onto the grid. Every model is kept, so fuel groups can be redrawn later without
   redoing this step.
2. **Ecoregions on the same grid.** Each cell takes the Level II ecoregion covering most of it;
   the few land cells outside every polygon (coast, lake shores) take the nearest one.
3. **Inventory of the units.** For every ecoregion × fuel group: land area, how many cells the
   group dominates, how many are "pure" (one group holds at least half, or three quarters, of the
   land), how many are in the strict herbaceous mask used for the satellite dates, how many NPN
   grass sites fall in that ecoregion and fuel group, and how many wildfires of 10 acres or more
   (2001–2024) burned there. Fires are attributed by the fuel shares of their 4 km cell, not by the
   fuel model at the fire's point: LANDFIRE 2023 shows the fuels after a fire, and reported fire
   locations are often approximate.

Fuel groups: **GR** grass, **GS** grass-shrub, **SH** shrub, **TU** timber-understory, **TL**
timber litter (SB slash-blowdown is rare). Cropland is nonburnable (NB3) in this fuel map, so it is
reported as its own group rather than dropped.

```{r eco-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Level II ecoregions: land area, burnable and agricultural shares, NPN grass sites and wildfires (>= 10 ac, 2001-2024)."
if (have) {
  x <- E[, c("code", "name", "land_km2", "share_burnable", "share_ag", "median_dom_share", "npn_sites", "fires")]
  x$land_km2 <- format(round(x$land_km2 / 1000), big.mark = ","); x$share_burnable <- sprintf("%.0f %%", 100 * x$share_burnable)
  x$share_ag <- sprintf("%.0f %%", 100 * x$share_ag); x$median_dom_share <- sprintf("%.2f", x$median_dom_share)
  names(x) <- c("Code", "Ecoregion", "Land (1,000 km²)", "Burnable", "Agriculture", "Median purity", "NPN sites", "Fires")
  knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrrrr")
} else cat("Table pending (run 71 and 79).")
```

```{r unit-counts, results="asis"}
if (have) {
  ub <- U[U$group %in% burn, ]
  n50 <- sum(ub$cells_p50 >= 50); n200 <- sum(ub$cells_p50 >= 200)
  gg <- ub[ub$group %in% c("GR", "GS"), ]
  cat(sprintf("\n**In numbers%s.** %d ecoregion × burnable-group units hold at least 50 cells where the group has half the land or more (%d at 200 cells). Of the grass and grass-shrub units, %d have at least one NPN grass site and %d have three or more.\n\n",
              prof_note, n50, n200, sum(gg$npn_sites > 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(gg$npn_sites >= 3, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
```

## Climatologies by unit (step 4)

**Decided (Oct 26, 2026).** Climatologies for grass (GR) and grass-shrub (GS) units in every Level II
ecoregion, plus shrub (SH) in the Cold Deserts, where shrub is extensive and overlaps the herbaceous
mask. A unit's cells are the 4 km cells where its fuel group holds at least half the land (three
quarters as a sensitivity check), and a unit needs at least 200 such cells (about 3,000 km²). Timber
groups are left out (the satellite sees the canopy, not the surface fuel), as is agriculture (crop
calendars, not fuel; reported above as context). Fire activity as a check on the units comes later,
as its own step.

**How.** For each cell, the typical date of each satellite season metric is its median over
2001–2025 (the same typical date as the regions work's rules package). A unit's typical date is the
median over its cells, with the spread across cells (25–75 %). Year-to-year spread comes from each
year's median departure across the unit's cells (departures over 90 days are left out as season
jumps). "Shared" is the share of the cells' year-to-year variation that the unit has in common: high
values mean the unit moves together, so a unit-level adjustment could work. NPN grass sites in the
usable record are matched to units by their ecoregion and fuel model; each site's date is the median
over its species. The unit's typical date is compared with the site's own 4 km cell's typical date, to
see how much a unit table loses against a per-cell map.

```{r clim-fig, results="asis"}
show_fig("ecofuel_climatology", "Typical green-up, NDVI peak and curing for each grass, grass-shrub and Cold Deserts shrub unit, with the spread across the unit's cells, NPN ground medians where a unit has three or more sites, and the year-to-year spread of curing.")
```

```{r clim-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Unit climatologies (cells where the group holds >= 50 % of the land). Dates are typical dates with the 25-75 % range across the unit's cells; year sd = year-to-year spread; shared = share of year-to-year variation common to the unit."
ctab <- function(name) {
  for (p in c("full", "dev")) { f <- sprintf("tables/ecofuel_clim_%s_%s.csv", name, p); if (file.exists(f)) return(utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) }
  NULL
}
CU <- ctab("units"); CC <- ctab("climatology"); CG <- ctab("ground_summary")
md <- function(d) ifelse(is.na(d), "–", format(as.Date("2001-01-01") + round(d) - 1, "%b %d"))
if (!is.null(CU) && !is.null(CC)) {
  CU <- CU[CU$eligible, ]; CC <- CC[CC$version == "p50", ]
  g <- function(u, m, f) { v <- CC[[f]][CC$unit == u & CC$metric == m]; if (length(v)) v[1] else NA }
  grp <- c(GR = "Grass", GS = "Grass-shrub", SH = "Shrub")
  x <- data.frame(
    Unit = sprintf("%s %s", CU$code, CU$name), Fuel = grp[CU$group], Cells = format(CU$cells, big.mark = ","),
    `Green-up` = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", md(g(u, "sos20", "typical")), md(g(u, "sos20", "q25")), md(g(u, "sos20", "q75")))),
    `Green-up year sd` = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) sprintf("%.0f d", g(u, "sos20", "yty_sd"))),
    Peak = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) md(g(u, "ndvi_peak_doy", "typical"))),
    Curing = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", md(g(u, "eos50", "typical")), md(g(u, "eos50", "q25")), md(g(u, "eos50", "q75")))),
    `Curing year sd` = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) sprintf("%.0f d", g(u, "eos50", "yty_sd"))),
    `Curing shared` = sapply(CU$unit, function(u) sprintf("%.2f", g(u, "eos50", "sync"))),
    check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrllllrr")
} else cat("Table pending (run 72 and 79).")
```

```{r ground-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Ground check: NPN grass sites in each unit. Bias = unit typical date minus ground date (median over sites); error = mean absolute difference using the unit's typical date vs the site's own 4 km cell's typical date."
if (!is.null(CG)) {
  z <- CG[CG$sites >= 3 | CG$unit == "all units", ]
  z <- z[order(z$unit == "all units", z$unit, z$target), ]
  x <- data.frame(Unit = z$unit, `Ground event` = z$target, `Satellite metric` = z$metric, Sites = z$sites,
                  `Ground median` = md(z$ground_median), `Satellite typical` = md(z$sat_typical),
                  Bias = sprintf("%+.0f d", z$bias), `Error, unit` = sprintf("%.0f d", z$mae_unit),
                  `Error, own cell` = sprintf("%.0f d", z$mae_cell), check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, align = "lllrllrrr")
} else cat("Ground check pending (72 on the laptop, where the NPN record lives).")
```

**First findings (Oct 26, 2026).**

- **26 units** qualify (152,642 cells): grass and grass-shrub across the Plains, deserts, Western
  Cordillera, Southwest highlands, California and the Southeast, plus Cold Deserts shrub.
- **Some units mix two seasons.** In the Cold and Warm Deserts, the Western Cordillera and the
  Everglades, a quarter to two fifths of a unit's cells have a typical curing date more than 60 days
  from the unit's typical date. In the Warm Deserts, grass greens up typically in early March and
  grass-shrub in mid-June: spring and monsoon seasons share these units. One typical date per unit
  hides that split.
- **Units don't move together much from year to year.** The year-to-year spread of a unit's curing
  date is 5–17 days in most units (about 30 days in the two small south Texas units), and only about
  a fifth of the cells' year-to-year variation is shared across a unit (0.04–0.42). That argues
  against unit-level weather adjustments, as the NPN study found at the ground.
- **The satellite dates are offset from the ground.** At NPN sites in these units, the satellite's
  green-up (20 % of the NDVI rise) comes about 26 days before the ground green-up, and its curing
  about 20 days after the ground's 50 % curing. Leaving out sites where the satellite and the ground
  pick different seasons (7–12 sites per event), the unit's typical curing date is about as good as
  the site's own 4 km cell (error 32 vs 29 days; correlation across sites 0.54 vs 0.52). For
  green-up the unit loses the spatial pattern within it (error 39 vs 30 days; correlation 0.18 vs
  0.84), so ecoregion × fuel units are too coarse for green-up.

## Does the split earn its keep? (step 5)

**Decided (Oct 26, 2026).** Before more work on the units, compare them with other ways of
grouping the same cells. Every grouping is scored on the same 4 km cells (those of the climatology
units), so the comparison is fair:

- **Level II ecoregion** alone, and **Level II × fuel** (the units above);
- the units **split by season** where their cells form two clusters of typical dates more than
  60 days apart (for example spring vs monsoon green-up), the smaller holding at least a tenth of
  the cells;
- the units split into **500 m elevation bands**;
- **Level III ecoregions**, alone and × fuel;
- the **climate regions** (A2, 13 regions) from the regions work, alone and × fuel.

Three scores: how much of the variation in the satellite's typical dates each grouping explains,
predicting each cell from its group's cells in other 2° blocks (so groupings that only fit their
own neighbourhood are penalised); how much of the cells' year-to-year variation each group shares;
and how well each grouping predicts the NPN ground dates, predicting each site from the other sites
in its group with nearby sites (within 10 km) held out.

```{r cmp-fig, results="asis"}
show_fig("ecofuel_compare", "How well each grouping of the cells explains satellite typical green-up and curing dates (held-out blocks), shares year-to-year variation, and predicts NPN ground dates (nearby sites held out). Arrows mark values below the axis.")
```

```{r cmp-table}
#| tbl-cap: "Grouping comparison. Satellite R2 = share of the variance of the cells' typical dates explained, predicting from other 2-degree blocks; shared = share of year-to-year variation common within groups; ground R2 = NPN site dates predicted from other sites in the group (sites within 10 km held out)."
mt <- function(name) { for (p in c("full", "dev")) { f <- sprintf("tables/ecofuel_cmp_%s_%s.csv", name, p); if (file.exists(f)) return(utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) }; NULL }
SA <- mt("satellite"); GDc <- mt("ground"); GNc <- mt("groupings")
if (!is.null(SA)) {
  glab <- c(eco2 = "Level II ecoregion", eco2_fuel = "Level II × fuel (units)", eco2_fuel_season = "Level II × fuel × season",
            eco2_fuel_elev = "Level II × fuel × 500 m elevation", eco3 = "Level III ecoregion", eco3_fuel = "Level III × fuel",
            a2 = "Climate regions (A2, 13)", a2_fuel = "Climate regions × fuel")
  gs <- intersect(names(glab), unique(SA$grouping))
  f2 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", sprintf("%.2f", x))
  sv <- function(g, m, f) SA[[f]][SA$grouping == g & SA$metric == m][1]
  gv <- function(g, t) if (is.null(GDc)) NA else { v <- GDc$cv_r2[GDc$grouping == g & GDc$target == t]; if (length(v)) v[1] else NA }
  x <- data.frame(Grouping = glab[gs], Groups = GNc$groups_domain[match(gs, GNc$grouping)],
                  `Sat. green-up R2` = f2(sapply(gs, sv, m = "sos20", f = "cv_r2")), `Sat. curing R2` = f2(sapply(gs, sv, m = "eos50", f = "cv_r2")),
                  `Shared, green-up` = f2(sapply(gs, sv, m = "sos20", f = "sync")), `Shared, curing` = f2(sapply(gs, sv, m = "eos50", f = "sync")),
                  `Ground green-up R2` = f2(sapply(gs, gv, t = "greenup")), `Ground curing R2` = f2(sapply(gs, gv, t = "curing")),
                  check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrr")
} else cat("Comparison pending (run 73 and 79).")
```

**What the comparison shows (Oct 27, 2026).**

- **Fuel type adds almost nothing.** Within Level II ecoregions, splitting by fuel group barely
  changes how much of the satellite timing is explained (green-up 0.19 → 0.22, curing 0.21 → 0.20),
  and on the ground it makes predictions worse: splitting the sites into more groups leaves fewer
  sites to learn from in each, and the fuel model at a site says little about its dates.
- **Finer geography does more.** Level III ecoregions explain about twice as much of the satellite
  timing as Level II (green-up 0.45, curing 0.58), more than the climate regions (0.29 and 0.49)
  with more groups (75 vs 13). Elevation bands within the units help less than Level III.
- **Units don't move together from year to year** under any grouping: a fifth to a third of the
  cells' year-to-year variation is shared (0.18–0.33).
- **On the ground, only green-up has a spatial pattern** that groupings can carry to new sites:
  Level III and the climate regions predict NPN green-up best (about 0.23–0.24 of the variance, with
  nearby sites held out); no grouping predicts ground curing better than the national median (88
  sites, mostly NEON).
- **The season split's satellite score is circular**, so it is not a fair test: each cell's season
  comes from its own typical satellite dates, the same dates it is then scored on. The two-season
  pattern is real (in the Warm Deserts, spring and monsoon seasons about four months apart), but what
  the split is worth needs a fair test, with the seasons taken from other years or from climate. On
  the ground, which is independent, it adds nothing.

## Still open

1. **Fire as a check on the units** (next step after the climatologies): the fire study's
   year-to-year test with these units in place of the climate regions, in the large western and
   Plains grass and grass-shrub units.
2. **Models** for units whose year-to-year variation is large and shared, with the ground check
   as the gate.
3. **LANDFIRE 2024** as a later sensitivity check.
